title: Cardinal-smallness consequences for a perfect derived class
statement: Let S be an essentially v-small replete triangulated class in D(A) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with coproducts [lem-grothendieck-derived-has-coproducts], closed under coproducts with fewer than regular alpha summands, and exactly the alpha-compact objects [def-sfb-alpha-compact-object]. Then S is perfect: componentwise surjectivity of Hom(U,f_i) for all U in S implies surjectivity of Hom(U,coproduct f_i). Every map from an object of S to a coproduct of objects of S factors through a subcoproduct which is still in S.

source.place: Bounded-subcoproduct factorization and perfectness: Krause Localization theory Sections 6.2-6.3 and Proposition 6.8.1.

proof.text: Transport the canonical G4 factorization across the equality characterizing S; lift each component by the assumed surjectivity and assemble its coproduct. This is the proved G4-implies-perfect API.
Apply alpha-smallness to obtain a support of size less than alpha. Closure of S under such coproducts puts the support coproduct in S; its inclusion gives the displayed factorization.

proof_origin.place: Source-correct alpha-compactness, Krause (2001) G3/G4, Lemmas 4--5; Neeman Theorem 0.2.

statement_change.old_statement: If S in a Grothendieck derived category is essentially small, replete and triangulated, is closed under coproducts indexed by types of cardinality less than a regular cardinal alpha, and every object of S is alpha-presentable, then componentwise surjectivity on Hom from S survives every v-small coproduct and every map from an object of S to a coproduct of S-objects factors through a subcoproduct in S.
statement_change.what: The source defines alpha-compactness by alpha-smallness and coproduct factorization G4, not ordinary IsCardinalPresentable in the triangulated category. The old ordinary-presentable theorem is not established by this repair; replace that erroneous interface by the actual source notion, with all consumers adapted in the same delivery. This restores the source proof without weakening the unchanged final perfect-class theorem. The old proof additionally depended on a false finite-support theorem; use G4 for perfectness and true alpha-small support for the second clause.

source.place: Krause (2001) pages 121--125, alpha-small objects and maximal G4 class; Localization theory 6.3 and 6.10.2 distinguish this from presentability in the abelianization.

citers.note: The downstream perfect-class conclusion is unchanged. The Core/Properties interfaces are adapted together to the actual maximal alpha-compact class; no target statement or target-used definition changes.

old_proof.text: Factor a map from an alpha-presentable object through a finite subcoproduct of the target family, using the finite-support factorization lemma.

For a finite subcoproduct, lift each component through the given componentwise surjections and reassemble the lifts by the finite biproduct lemma; transport the lift along the subcoproduct inclusions.
Apply the factorization lemma to a map into a coproduct of S-objects and use closure of S under subcoproducts.
